mode_note: Per recipe-feature-pipeline orchestrator instruction, synth-substrate operates in implementation-strategy mode for this pipeline; the three-option enumeration hard exclusion in substrate-translation-knowledge SKILL.md does NOT apply. Option count is justified by genuine option space, not by quota. Straw-men dropped. Decisions whose PRD framing explicitly names a rejected branch (e.g., D-0001 OI-A1) enumerate the rejected branch so downstream design-composer sees why it was not chosen.
registry_version: n/a (implementation-strategy mode; no substrate registry consulted — target substrate is claude_code throughout)
framer_lean_check: For each decision the framer recorded a recommendation_strength (strong / moderate / weak / route-to-gate) and a preferred option in options_summary. This file's recommended_option is checked against that lean and any divergence is surfaced under recommendation_divergence at the end.

mappings.title: OI-A1: Prescription extraction path for FR-1 design-realization audits

options.name: companion_file
options.description: Sibling YAML/JSON file next to each ADR-*.md (e.g., ADR-0042.prescriptions.yaml) listing the ADR's machine-checkable predicates: invariants, must-hold-after-implementation assertions, file-pattern guards. The architecture auditor reads the companion as the canonical prescription source; ADR prose remains canonical for the decision narrative per ADR-0036 / ADR-0056. Companion file MUST NOT duplicate the decision; only its check-shaped predicates.
pros: 9/9 surveyed production systems use this shape (T-002 cross-source triple; C-0034-T002, C-0239, C-0246).
Avoids the documented 44.57% LLM misinterpretation rate on NLP-parse of decision prose (arXiv 2602.07609 via C-0239).
Predicates are reviewable in PR diff like any other artifact; cheap to lint with schema validation.
Decouples audit-tooling evolution from ADR-prose evolution — schema changes to predicates do not require ADR re-issuance.
cons: Establishes a new repo convention; no *.yaml siblings to ADR-*.md exist today (C-0136). Authoring burden landed onto ADR authors at write time.
Risk of divergence: companion-file drifts from ADR prose. Mitigation: auditing-shared script that diffs the companion against the ADR's machine-checkable section and flags mismatch.
Legacy ADR backfill required — ADR-0001..ADR-0056 currently lack companions; either backfill incrementally or scope FR-1 audit to new ADRs only with a deprecation window.
evidence_anchors: C-0154 (Discovery does not pre-decide; routes for human resolution)
preconditions: Companion-file schema authored as part of FR-1 work (host: .claude/skills/KB-review-disciplines/architecture-audit.md or new auditing-shared reference).
ADR template extended with a 'See companion: <path>' pointer line (does not violate ADR-0056 because companion is reference, not carve-out).
Deprecation window for legacy ADRs documented in §O posture (event-triggered trigger: 'when an FR-1 audit hits an ADR without a companion').

cost.maintenance_burden: moderate (ADR authors must author companion at decision time; one-time backfill for high-value legacy ADRs)
cost.irreversibility_cost: moderate (companions exist in adrs/; removing requires retracting and migrating to NLP-parse — but companions are passive metadata, not load-bearing schemas)

options.name: nlp_parse_adr_prose
options.description: Architecture auditor extracts prescriptions from ADR prose at audit time using LLM-based parsing. Operates on the canonical ADR body (no new file convention). Audit fidelity depends on prose conventions (ADR template adherence, sentence-form discipline).
pros: No new convention; ADR template unchanged.
Inherits ADR-0036 (single canonical location) and ADR-0056 (no carve-outs) naturally — the canonical decision is what gets parsed.
cons: Peer-reviewed misinterpretation rate of 44.57% on the exact category 'semantic/logical misinterpretation' (arXiv 2602.07609 via C-0239). Above NFR thresholds for any reasonable audit signal.
0/9 surveyed production systems use this shape (T-002).
Audit non-determinism: parsing the same ADR twice can yield different prescription sets — falsifies the audit's repeatability gate.

Single-sourced FP claim weakness (C-0239 not externally re-fetched in Critic sweep) is a small risk, but the qualitative argument 'NLP-parse of decision prose is fragile' is corroborated by Rosik 2011 (C-0246) and the 0/9 vendor convergence.
evidence_anchors: C-0137 (NLP path operates on canonical prose, inherits ADR-0036/0056)

cost.runtime_overhead: significant (LLM call per audited ADR; auditor model time)
cost.maintenance_burden: high (every ADR template change risks parse regression; prompt tuning becomes infrastructure)
cost.irreversibility_cost: low (NLP-parse code can be replaced by companion-file reader without retraction)

options.rejection_rationale: Documented 44.57% misinterpret rate (C-0239) and 0/9 surveyed precedent (T-002) make this path uncompetitive. PRD-v2 OI-A1 explicitly named both branches, so this branch is enumerated for design-composer visibility per framer instruction.

options.name: hybrid_nlp_drafting_companion_canonical
options.description: NLP-parse used at ADR draft time to surface a starter set of machine-checkable predicates; ADR author reviews and ratifies into companion-file. Audit reads the companion as canonical. NLP becomes an authoring assist; not an audit input.
pros: Reduces companion-authoring burden (the dominant con of pure companion_file).
Lowers the legacy backfill cost: pass legacy ADRs through NLP-draft + author-review.
Audit canonicality remains the human-ratified companion, so the 44.57% misinterpret rate does NOT bleed into the audit signal.
cons: Two-system maintenance burden: NLP draft tooling AND companion-file schema both need ongoing ownership.
Drift risk if authors over-trust the NLP-drafted starter set and under-review (anti-pattern: rubber-stamping).
Higher initial effort than pure companion_file.
evidence_anchors: C-0239 (NLP misinterpret rate isolated to drafting, not audit)
preconditions: Same as companion_file plus prompt template + author-review checklist.

cost.runtime_overhead: none at audit time; LLM call at draft time only

options.note: Worth considering if the legacy-ADR backfill cost in companion_file proves too high in practice. Not recommended for the initial implementation — adds complexity for a problem (authoring burden) that does not exist until the backfill workload is observed. Defer to a future iteration if the ADR-author burden NFR is breached.

mappings.rationale: 9/9 surveyed precedent + peer-reviewed counter-evidence on the rejected branch + low blast radius. The hybrid is the natural escape hatch if authoring burden bites; not needed up-front. The rejected NLP-only path is enumerated solely because PRD-v2's OI-A1 wording explicitly named it.

mappings.title: OI-A2: FR-3 PV-tier cross-file invariant authoring shape
mappings.framer_lean: hybrid (denormalized declaration, centralized body) (strong; externally_decided: true)

options.name: hybrid_denormalized_declaration_centralized_body
options.description: Each PV declares which invariants it owns/honors at the artifact (denormalized declaration: a YAML stanza or markdown table at the PV header). The invariant body — predicate logic, error message text, severity — lives in a central catalog (e.g., .claude/skills/KB-task-decomposition/cross-file-invariants.md). Declarations reference catalog entries by ID; catalog hosts the reusable predicates.
pros: 6/6 surveyed systems land here as the documented sweet spot (T-004; C-0367).
Shopify Packwerk retrospective (C-0350, C-0352, C-0365, C-0366) is the strongest available counter to fully-centralized — and it's preempted by this hybrid choice.
Locality at declaration site (PV authors see what they own); DRY at body site (one place to change the predicate).
Cross-file invariants by definition need cross-file coordination — central body is structurally appropriate.
cons: Two-file coordination at edit time (declaration site + catalog).
Catalog grows monotonically; needs a deprecation discipline for invariants that fall out of use.
T-004's caveat: surveyed domain is code/data/API, not pipeline-document content (open question 1 of T-004). Transferability is a design judgment.
C-0366 'different teams' framing is T-004 author gloss (partially_verified).
preconditions: Catalog host file authored (KB-task-decomposition/cross-file-invariants.md or sibling).
Invariant-ID convention established (e.g., CFI-<NNN>).
Test-phase-validator-author rubric (PV-author rubric host) consumes the catalog.

cost.maintenance_burden: moderate (catalog grows; PV authors learn declare-then-reference idiom)
cost.irreversibility_cost: low-moderate (hybrid is composable: collapse to centralized by inlining declarations, or to denormalized by absorbing bodies into PVs)

options.name: denormalized_inline
options.description: Each PV declares and defines its invariants in-line. No central catalog. Best locality; worst DRY.
pros: Maximum locality — everything a PV reader needs is in the PV file.
No catalog dependency; no cross-file coordination at edit time.
ArchUnit-style: rule-with-test (T-002 caveat at C-0034-T002 line 149).
cons: Same invariant defined N times across N PVs → drift risk (cross-file invariants are by definition shared).
Severity / error-message text scattered — vocabulary divergence (see D-0010) worsens.
Catalog gives a single audit anchor; inline loses it.
evidence_anchors: C-0367 (denormalized is one extreme of the surveyed axis; no surveyed system is fully-extremed but Terraform and Bazel lean denormalized)

cost.irreversibility_cost: moderate (extracting central bodies later is mechanical but PV-by-PV)

options.rejection_rationale: Cross-file invariants without a central body invite per-PV drift. The point of FR-3 (mechanism H9) is to enforce cross-file consistency — denormalized-inline structurally fights the goal.

options.name: centralized
options.description: Single catalog file owns all invariants. PVs do not declare; the catalog declares which PVs each invariant applies to. PV files are silent about their invariant surface.
pros: Maximum DRY — one place to look.
Easy global audit pass: read catalog, derive PV coverage.
cons: Shopify Packwerk retrospective (C-0350, C-0352, C-0365): tried-centralized, walked back. Privacy checks removed in Packwerk v3.0 (C-0352).
PV authors lose locality: cannot read a PV file and know what invariants it owes without cross-referencing the catalog.
Catalog becomes a bottleneck artifact — every PV change risks a catalog edit by a different owner (C-0366 framing).
JSON Schema $defs is per-document, not cross-document (C-0367); the closest-to-centralized surveyed pattern stops short of fully-cross-document central.

cost.maintenance_burden: high (catalog becomes choke point per Packwerk lesson)
cost.irreversibility_cost: high (the explicit lesson of Packwerk is that walking back is costly)

options.rejection_rationale: Strongest available counter-example (Packwerk migration retrospective) goes through this exact path and walks back. Even with T-004's caveat about transferability, the negative signal is preserved across the analogical mapping.

mappings.rationale: 6/6 surveyed sweet spot + the only documented migration retrospective in the corpus goes through centralized and walks back. The two rejected options are both surveyed extremes and both have explicit failure modes documented.

mappings.title: OI-A3: Scope of auditing-skills reverse-check
mappings.framer_lean: separate rule on auditing-skills (weak; externally_decided: false; low blast radius)

options.name: separate_rule_in_auditing_skills
options.description: Author a new reverse-check rule inside .claude/skills/auditing-skills/ that mirrors FR-10's SA-13 (sub-agent → owning skill family back-reference) at the skill level (skill file → owning agent or recipe back-reference). One small rule file; one new audit dimension.
pros: Separation of concerns: auditing-subagents covers agent-side reverse refs; auditing-skills covers skill-side. Each audit family stays internally coherent.
Low blast radius (one new rule file under one skill family).
Reversible — rule can be relaxed or removed if the audit gap doesn't materialize.
Makes the §O posture for FR-11 cleaner: each posture decision attaches to its own audit family without cross-family conditional logic.
cons: Externally undecided — no T-001..T-004 corroborator; rests on internal Discovery reasoning only (C-0123, C-0131).
Two audit families end up with structurally-similar rules; if either evolves, manual sync risk.
evidence_anchors: C-0091 (auditing-skills family carries its own conventions)
preconditions: Rule wording mirrors SA-13 phrasing for cross-family symmetry.

options.name: extend_fr10_scope_to_cover_auditing_skills
options.description: FR-10's rule explicitly enumerates both auditing-subagents AND auditing-skills as in-scope surfaces. One rule, two surfaces.
pros: Single rule definition; no cross-family sync risk.
Simpler PRD-level traceability.
cons: Couples two audit families to one rule change cadence — if auditing-subagents evolves the SA-13 shape, auditing-skills inherits the change unintentionally.
FR-10 was scoped narrowly in PRD-v2; broadening here drifts from the framer's lean.
options.note: Defensible if design-composer prefers minimum-surface-area FR scope. Not recommended because the framer's separation-of-concerns lean is the cleaner architectural choice and the cost delta is negligible.

options.name: defer
options.description: Ship FR-10 alone for now; revisit auditing-skills reverse-check only if the audit gap is observed in practice. Document the deferral in §O posture (event-triggered: 'when an FR-10 audit miss surfaces a skill-side reverse-ref gap').
pros: Lowest immediate cost.
Honest about the externally-undecided status (no T-corroborator).
Consistent with §O event-triggered posture for FR-11.
cons: Leaves an asymmetric audit surface in the meantime.
Adds another deferral to the register, which competes with the goal of FR-11 (replace post-ship felt-utility with event-triggered triggers — adding deferrals can become its own ritual).
preconditions: Deferral entry in Issues/devcontainer-mcp-provisioning-r1-deferrals/register.md or a successor.
options.note: Acceptable fallback if design-composer wants to compress FR scope. The framer's preference for the separate rule is grounded in symmetry, not urgency.

mappings.rationale: Symmetric audit surfaces; low cost; reversible. The two viable alternatives are both defensible and cheap — design-composer can substitute either without re-architecting the rest of the feature.

mappings.title: OI-A5: Blocks-X marker grammar
mappings.framer_lean: structured marker / pragma (moderate; n=1 prior occurrence — establishment not reconciliation)

options.name: structured_html_comment_pragma
options.description: Adopt a structured machine-parseable marker: `<!-- BLOCKS: <stage-slug>-completion -->` (or YAML token list inside) embedded in Discovery output. Single canonical shape, parsed by the gate/validator cluster.
pros: n=1 prior occurrence means no grammar to honor — establishing a structured shape now costs nothing in compatibility.
HTML comments are invisible in rendered markdown but greppable from CI.
Structured shape supports multi-slug from day one ('BLOCKS: stage-a-completion, stage-b-completion').
Downstream consumers (FR-2 conformance schema, AC-FR-9-* assertions, FR-3 PV-tier invariants) inherit a stable wire format.
Easier mechanical evaluator for D-0005's predicate.
cons: Diverges from the n=1 prose precedent ('Blocks <stage-slug>-completion.') — a tiny migration if the prior occurrence is retained anywhere.
Slight authoring overhead (Discovery output authors must use the pragma form).
Lock-in if downstream FR-2 ships before grammar revision.
preconditions: Grammar spec hosted in .claude/skills/KB-documentation-criteria/ (or sibling).
FR-2 conformance schema references the pragma form.

cost.irreversibility_cost: moderate (downstream consumers harden against the shape after FR-2 ships)

options.name: yaml_frontmatter_field
options.description: Add a `blocks:` field to Discovery output frontmatter (YAML list of stage slugs). Pure structured data; no inline prose marker.
pros: Strongest structured shape — list semantics native.
Trivially parseable by any YAML reader.
cons: Discovery output is not currently frontmatter-bearing for this kind of metadata (would need a schema extension).
Less discoverable in prose review — readers skim body text, not frontmatter.
Most over-engineered relative to n=1 precedent.
Imposes frontmatter discipline on Discovery output authors who currently write free-form analysis prose.
preconditions: Discovery output frontmatter schema authored.
options.note: Acceptable if design-composer prefers maximum structure; not recommended because it over-engineers relative to the n=1 baseline and the pragma form already supports multi-slug.

options.name: preserve_n1_prose_grammar_verbatim
options.description: Adopt the existing n=1 prose grammar verbatim ('Blocks <stage-slug>-completion.') as canonical. Parser uses a regex.
pros: Zero migration: the one existing occurrence is canonical.
Human-readable in prose context.
cons: Single-slug only by construction — multi-stage blocks require parser ambiguity (multiple sentences? comma list?). Either way, regex grows.
Period-terminated kebab-case is a documentation-discipline rule expressed as natural language; brittle to grammar variation ('Blocks the stage-x-completion.' would fail).
Premature lock-in to a precedent of n=1 that itself was not designed as a grammar.

cost.irreversibility_cost: high (downstream hardens against a fragile shape)

options.rejection_rationale: n=1 is not a grammar — it's an occurrence. Honoring it verbatim ossifies a parser that was never designed. The structured pragma form preserves the readable intent (the `BLOCKS:` token is still skim-greppable) without the regex fragility.

mappings.rationale: n=1 prior occurrence is not a grammar to honor — it's a starting point. Structured pragma is greppable, multi-slug-ready, invisible in rendered output, and cheap. Frontmatter is over-engineered; verbatim prose lock-in is fragile.

mappings.title: OI-A6: Mechanical evaluator for FR-6 trigger conditions 3 and 4

options.name: hybrid_advisory_predicate_with_human_ratification
options.description: A mechanical predicate scans Blueprint's Skill-Coverage Decisions section for trigger-shaped tokens (e.g., 'new skill proposed', 'cross-skill impact noted') and surfaces an advisory annotation at the Design Composition gate. design-composer (human) ratifies whether the matrix is required. Predicate false-negatives surface as human override events logged to state-transitions.log.
pros: Balances mechanical determinism with human judgment on interpretive triggers (3 and 4).
Couples cleanly with D-0008 (substance-not-presence heuristic) — the predicate looks for shape; the human checks substance.
Logs override events for retrospective: if the predicate's false-negative rate is high, it gets tightened; if low, it can be promoted to mandatory.
Cheap to ship; cheap to tune.
cons: Two-system maintenance (predicate code + human-checklist).
Externally undecided — no T-001..T-004 corroborator on trigger-evaluation pattern.
Risk of the human ratification becoming a rubber stamp (anti-pattern), undermining the predicate's value.
preconditions: Predicate hosted in .claude/skills/auditing-subagents/ (mechanical evaluator host).
design-claude-code.md procedure has a ratification step at Design Composition gate.
state-transitions.log entry shape extended for override events (auditing-shared/log_state_transition.py).

options.name: machine_checkable_predicate_only
options.description: Pure mechanical predicate gates the matrix-mandatory check. Trigger 3 and 4 evaluated by token-pattern match in Blueprint's Skill-Coverage Decisions section. No human checkpoint.
pros: Deterministic; auditable.
Fastest gate (no human-in-loop).
cons: Triggers 3 and 4 are interpretive — pattern-match brittleness yields false negatives ('cross-skill impact' phrased five different ways).
Conflicts with D-0008's substance-not-presence heuristic (the predicate checks presence of phrasing, not substance of intent).
Single point of failure: a missed trigger is silently un-audited.
options.rejection_rationale: Interpretive triggers do not survive predicate-only enforcement; the documented FR-7 anti-ritualism trade-off (T-003, C-0257) applies symmetrically here — checking phrasing is presence-not-substance.

options.name: human_in_loop_only_at_design_composition_gate
options.description: design-composer (human) checks Blueprint's Skill-Coverage Decisions section at Design Composition gate; no mechanical evaluator. Trigger 3 and 4 are judgment calls every time.
pros: Highest signal fidelity on interpretive triggers.
No false-negative chase; no maintenance burden on a predicate.
Coheres with FR-7's substance-not-presence framing (D-0008).
cons: Highest ritual cost — every Design Composition repeats the check.
No advisory annotation to focus attention; reviewer reads the whole section every time.
Inconsistent application across runs (reviewer-dependent).
evidence_anchors: C-0046/C-0078/C-0079 (Design Composition gate is the human-checkpoint surface today)
options.note: Defensible if design-composer prefers zero-tool-debt. Not recommended because the advisory predicate is cheap and directly reduces reviewer cognitive load without claiming the predicate is authoritative.

mappings.rationale: Predicate-only loses signal on interpretive triggers; human-only wastes reviewer attention on shape-checks the machine can pre-filter. The hybrid pairs cheap pre-screening with authoritative human ratification and logs overrides for tuning.
mappings.cross_decision_dependency: Couples to D-0008 (substance-not-presence heuristic for W/H/A trifecta). The predicate here must NOT score substance; it scores shape only.

mappings.title: OI-A4 / Contingency Split: R1 single feature vs R2a/R2b split
mappings.decision_class_note: Framer marked this 'route-to-gate' — design-cc cannot ratify alone. This synth-substrate entry preserves both readings as admissible inputs to Gate 4 without recommending one.

options.name: orchestrators_currently_open_reading_6_ois
options.description: Count only currently-open OIs (PRD-v2 OI-A1..OI-A6 = 6). Threshold of 12 (PRD §Contingency Split §1) is NOT tripped. Ship as R1 single feature.
pros: Reflects the synthesis-stage view: IC OIs (8) are resolved upstream; PRD-v2 OIs (6) are the live count.
Avoids the one-way irreversibility cost of splitting (split downstream requires re-merging artifacts).
Coheres with orchestrator's current routing posture.
cons: Disregards the codebase researcher's cumulative reading — IC OIs are cumulative inputs to the run, not closed-and-discarded.
If the threshold's intent is 'cumulative run-load', this reading under-counts.
preconditions: design-composer at Gate 4 ratifies the 6-count reading as the operative one.

cost.irreversibility_cost: low (does not split; can split later if R2b cluster proves overloaded)

options.framer_note: Per framer instruction: orchestrator's reading prevails for this run absent contradicting evidence at Gate 4. Not 'recommended' in the design-cc sense because this is not a design-cc decision.

options.name: codebase_researchers_cumulative_reading_14_ois
options.description: Count cumulative open items (8 IC + 6 PRD-v2 = 14). Threshold of 12 IS tripped mechanically per C-0004/C-0005/C-0145. Split into R2a (FR-1, FR-6, FR-7, FR-8, FR-9, FR-10) and R2b (FR-2, FR-3, FR-4, FR-5, FR-11) per mechanism-dependency clusters (C-0125, C-0126, C-0127).
pros: Mechanical reading of the threshold text ('cumulative count of open items exceeds 12').
Cluster boundaries are evidence-grounded (C-0114, C-0116, C-0125, C-0126, C-0127 verified).
Conservative — splits early, before R1 grows unmanageable.
cons: One-way decision — undoing requires re-merging downstream artifacts at high cost.
May be over-conservative if IC OIs are in fact closed-and-discarded.
Coordination cost of two parallel runs (R2a + R2b).
preconditions: design-composer at Gate 4 ratifies the cumulative reading.
R2a/R2b cluster scopes formally adopted from the mechanism-dependency table.

cost.maintenance_burden: n/a (decision-only; downstream cost is the split itself)

options.framer_note: Both readings are well-evidenced; this one is admissible if Gate 4 surfaces evidence (e.g., R1 design-time scope exceeds reviewer capacity) that contradicts the orchestrator's reading.

mappings.rationale: Per framer's 'route-to-gate' status and per C-0006 ('design-composer must apply the threshold mechanically at Gate 4'). This synth-substrate entry preserves both readings; design-composer ratifies at Gate 4. Absent contradicting evidence, the orchestrator's 6-OI reading prevails per framer instruction.

mappings.title: FR-5: Four-stage drift-detection pipeline
mappings.framer_lean: four-stage pipeline (RFC 8785 → baseline → RFC 6902 → severity catalog) (strong; externally_decided: true)

options.name: four_stage_pipeline
options.description: Stage 1: RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS) normalizes tools/list payloads. Stage 2: persisted canonical baseline (oasdiff change-fingerprint pattern; baseline-as-bytes). Stage 3: RFC 6902 JSON-Patch diff with identity-keyed array diff (tool name is unique per MCP spec). Stage 4: locally-enumerated severity catalog modeled on oasdiff (remove → BLOCKER per AC-FR-5-a; signature change → MAJOR per AC-FR-5-e; addition → MINOR per AC-FR-5-d; description/title/icon → INFO).
pros: Strong cross-source triple (T-001): each stage grounded in an independent primary (RFC 8785, oasdiff fingerprint, RFC 6902, oasdiff catalog).
FP-suppression located where the evidence supports it: normalization (step 1) + catalog routing (step 4), not diff defaults (per C-0195 and openapi-diff Issue #673 cautionary tale).
Identity-keyed array diff is grounded in MCP spec — tools have unique names (E-0055).
Composable: each stage is replaceable without re-architecting the others.
cons: <5% FP claim (NFR-4) is single-sourced (C-0201, C-0202); no primary measures the exact FP rate under these conditions. Mechanism is well-argued but the number is extrapolated.
Composition step (oasdiff catalog → MCP tools/list) is novel — single-sourced in T-001 but defensible because each underlying primitive is well-cited.
Pilot validation required at Phase Validator time to confirm <5% FP target.
preconditions: RFC 8785 JCS reference implementation selected (Python: e.g., rfc8785 package or in-tree pure-stdlib implementation).
Canonical baseline storage location (auditing-mcp/ subdir; one file per MCP server).
RFC 6902 JSON-Patch generator (jsonpatch library; identity-keyed array option configured for tools/list).
Severity catalog YAML hosted under auditing-mcp/references/ (or sibling).
Pilot run at Phase Validator time: 50 audits against stable upstreams; measure FP rate; refine catalog if >5%.

cost.cost_breakdown: JCS normalizer 0.5w (stdlib or one-line lib) + baseline storage + read/write 0.5w + RFC 6902 diff with identity-key config 0.5w + severity catalog authoring + integration 1w. Ongoing: catalog tuning as new MCP servers register.
cost.runtime_overhead: minor (4 sequential transforms on a ~10-100KB JSON payload per audit; sub-second)
cost.maintenance_burden: moderate (severity catalog evolves with MCP spec changes)

options.name: naive_object_diff_with_heuristic_severity
options.description: Direct object-diff over raw tools/list JSON; severity inferred at audit time by ad-hoc heuristics (e.g., key-name pattern matching).
pros: Simplest possible implementation.
No baseline storage required.
cons: openapi-diff Issue #673 is the documented cautionary tale — diff defaults miss real changes (C-0195).
Without normalization, formatting differences (key ordering, whitespace, number representation) become false positives — fails NFR-4 (<5% FP) on any realistic upstream.
Description-polishing and CDN-URL rewrites (C-0202) read as drift, not as INFO — naive heuristics will mis-route.
Heuristic severity is per-author per-audit — no auditable contract.
options.rejection_rationale: openapi-diff Issue #673 is the documented evidence that naive diff fails the exact use case. Cheap up front; expensive in steady-state.

options.name: vendor_tool_reuse_oasdiff_or_openapi_diff
options.description: Adopt oasdiff or openapi-diff directly, configured for MCP tools/list.
pros: Mature tools; battle-tested on OpenAPI surfaces.
No bespoke pipeline to author.
cons: Neither tool natively understands the MCP tools/list schema — they target OpenAPI / Swagger.
Adapter layer (translate MCP tools/list → OpenAPI-shaped doc → vendor diff → translate severity back) is more code than the bespoke four-stage pipeline AND inherits vendor-tool quirks.
openapi-diff Issue #673 is the documented quirk; reusing it inherits it.
evidence_anchors: C-0193 (vendor tools as model, not adopt)
options.rejection_rationale: Vendor tools target a different schema; the adapter cost exceeds the bespoke-pipeline cost while inheriting the vendor's known failure modes. T-001 explicitly cites oasdiff as a model, not a target for adoption.

mappings.rationale: Strong cross-source triple; each stage well-cited; novel composition is defensible because each primitive is sound. Two rejected alternatives have documented failure modes (Issue #673; vendor-tool schema mismatch).
loss_summary: pattern_fidelity: none (each stage is the surveyed primitive)
mappings.open_sub_decision: NFR-4 (<5% FP) measurement strategy. T-001 surfaces that no surveyed source publishes a quantitative benchmark; C-0201/C-0202 are single-sourced hypotheses. Recommend pilot run as hypothesis-validation at Phase Validator time — 50 audits against stable upstream MCP servers; refine catalog if measured FP > 5%.

mappings.title: FR-7: W/H/A trifecta as substance vs mandate

options.name: substance_as_rubric_with_mandate_for_new_skill_proposals
options.description: W/H/A is the substance reviewers check for (need-justification / scope-lifecycle hygiene / anti-pattern defenses per T-003's 3-category convergence). Reviewers apply a substance-not-presence heuristic: the trifecta is satisfied if the substance is present, regardless of whether three labelled headings exist. EXCEPTION: when a new skill is proposed, a structured W/H/A artifact is mandated (because new-skill proposals carry higher review cost and explicit shape lowers it). For all other concept introductions, the substance principle governs.
pros: Preserves T-003's cross-platform-convergent substance without inheriting the novel-ritualism risk (C-0257 explicitly identifies the codification-as-mandate as the novel and risky move).
Reviewer cost is lowered exactly where it's highest (new-skill proposals are the most expensive review surface).
Substance heuristic aligns with how reviewers actually catch missing rationale — substance-checking, not heading-counting.
Coheres with D-0005's advisory-predicate design (machine checks shape; human checks substance).
cons: Substance heuristic is harder to mechanically evaluate — reviewer-dependent.
Drawing the new-skill-proposal boundary requires a clear definition (what counts as 'new'?).
Quantitative BFCL evidence (C-0293: 96% → 13-15%) is single-sourced and directional, not measured threshold for this pipeline.
evidence_anchors: C-0257 (codification-as-mandate is the novel move; ritualism risk)
preconditions: KB-cc-design hosts the W/H/A rubric + substance heuristic.
design-claude-code.md procedure references the rubric at skill-coverage decision time.
'New skill proposal' boundary defined (likely: 'creates a new directory under .claude/skills/').

options.name: mandate_as_artifact_universally
options.description: Every skill-coverage decision MUST produce a structured W/H/A artifact with three labelled headings. Reviewer checks presence.
pros: Maximum auditability — easy to gate (does the artifact exist? does it have three headings?).
Removes reviewer judgment on shape.
cons: 0/6 surveyed platforms mandate this (C-0257) — novel-ritualism risk explicitly identified by T-003.
Presence-not-substance: three filled headings can be empty of content and still pass the gate.
Drives authors toward ritualistic minimum-viable filings, undermining the actual goal (need-justification + scope hygiene + anti-pattern awareness).

cost.irreversibility_cost: moderate (relaxing a mandate is harder than tightening a principle)

options.rejection_rationale: T-003 explicitly identifies the codification-as-mandate as the novel and risky move (anti-ritualism trade-off at C-0257 / T-003 line 177). 0/6 surveyed platforms mandate. The recommended hybrid captures the substance without the ritual.

options.name: principle_only_no_mandate
options.description: W/H/A is a principle in KB-cc-design; reviewers apply substance heuristic to all skill-coverage decisions including new-skill proposals. No mandate anywhere.
pros: Lightest authorial burden.
Maximum substance preservation (no ritual).
cons: Loses the audit anchor for new-skill proposals — the most expensive review surface gets the least structure.
Higher reviewer cognitive load on new-skill proposals where structure is most valuable.
Drift risk: principle without occasional structured artifact tends to fade in practice.
options.note: Defensible if design-composer wants zero structural artifacts. Not recommended because the new-skill-proposal carve-out is where structure pays for itself.

mappings.rationale: Preserves T-003 cross-source-convergent substance; respects the documented anti-ritualism trade-off; concentrates structural mandate where it has the highest review-cost ROI. Couples cleanly with D-0005's predicate-checks-shape / human-checks-substance split.
mappings.cross_decision_dependency: Couples to D-0005 (the advisory predicate there scores shape, not substance).

mappings.title: FR-11 §O posture placement
mappings.framer_lean: all-three-host placement (KB-cc-design + PV-author rubric + KB-documentation-criteria deferral conventions) (moderate)
mappings.design_composer_routing: E-2 inclusion scope routes to design-composer per C-0153.

options.name: three_host_placement_kb_cc_design_plus_pv_author_rubric_plus_kb_documentation_criteria
options.description: Place §O wording (event-triggered / honest-acceptance / concrete-machinery framings) in three host surfaces: (a) KB-cc-design — Principle 9 placement for cc-layer designers; (b) PV-author rubric in test-phase-validator-author — for PV authors who decide deferral framings; (c) KB-documentation-criteria — deferral conventions section so all discipline texts share the same posture grammar. Apply to discipline texts identified by §O.1 register (currently 5 rows: A-3, D-5, E-2, E-3, I-1) pending design-composer's E-2-inclusion scope decision.
pros: Purely additive — zero 'post-ship' precedent in .claude/skills/ and .claude/agents/ today (per Discovery). No collision risk.
Three hosts cover three audiences (cc-layer designers, PV authors, discipline-text authors) without cross-host conditional logic.
Coheres with the FR-11 goal: replace post-ship felt-utility with event-triggered / honest-acceptance / concrete-machinery.
Each host owns its surface — clean ownership boundaries.
cons: Three-host placement means three locations to keep coherent (sync risk).
E-2 inclusion is a separate sub-decision routed to design-composer (C-0153) — this option preempts neither inclusion nor exclusion.
Partially-verified count mismatch (C-0033: 4-row PRD AC-FR-11-c vs 5-row §O.1 register) means the exact discipline-text set depends on design-composer's ratification.
evidence_anchors: C-0110/C-0113 (zero post-ship precedent in current skills/agents)
preconditions: design-composer ratifies E-2-inclusion scope (independent sub-decision per C-0153).
KB-cc-design Principle 9 wording authored.
PV-author rubric extended with the three postures.
KB-documentation-criteria deferral-conventions section added.

cost.maintenance_burden: low (sync risk is small because all three hosts cite the same posture vocabulary)

options.name: kb_cc_design_only
options.description: Place §O wording in KB-cc-design only. PV-author rubric and KB-documentation-criteria do not directly host the postures.
pros: Lowest sync cost (one host).
Smallest blast radius.
cons: PV authors and discipline-text authors must derive postures from a cc-design-skill they may not read.
Underuses the additive opportunity — there's no precedent to honor and no cost to broadening placement.
options.note: Acceptable minimum-scope choice. Not recommended because broadening costs almost nothing and the additive opportunity is high.

options.name: kb_cc_design_plus_pv_author_rubric
options.description: Two-host placement: KB-cc-design and PV-author rubric. Discipline-text authors derive postures via KB-cc-design or PV-author rubric (whichever they consult).
pros: Covers the two primary author audiences (designers + PV authors).
Lower sync surface than three-host.
cons: Discipline-text authors (Issues/, Issues/*/register.md) lose the dedicated reference in KB-documentation-criteria.
Minor coverage gap relative to three-host.
options.note: Acceptable middle path. Not recommended because adding KB-documentation-criteria costs ~0.5w and meaningfully improves discipline-text-author guidance.

mappings.rationale: Purely additive (zero post-ship prose currently in target surfaces); three-host covers three distinct audiences; sync risk is minimal because all hosts share the same posture vocabulary. The two-host and one-host alternatives are admissible if design-composer wants to compress scope.
mappings.open_sub_decision: E-2 inclusion in AC-FR-11-c scope (routes to design-composer per C-0153). This decision selects the placement strategy; the row set is design-composer's call.

mappings.title: Severity vocabulary reconciliation across FR-1/FR-4/FR-5/FR-9/FR-10
mappings.framer_lean: preserve trifecta with explicit bridge table (moderate)
mappings.decision_owner_note: design-composer (cross-cuts layers); design-cc proposes for the cc layer.

options.name: preserve_trifecta_with_explicit_bridge_table
options.description: Each surface keeps its current vocabulary (auditor BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR/NIT; reviewer critical/important/recommended; phase-validator blocking/warning/informational). A bridge table — authored by design-composer and hosted in KB-review-disciplines/severity-taxonomy.md (or auditing-shared/ as the cross-surface utility host) — documents the cross-vocabulary mapping with explicit notes on non-monotonic edges (e.g., BLOCKER → critical → blocking is monotonic; NIT → recommended is borderline).
pros: Each vocabulary serves a different audience: auditor output drives tooling (numeric verdict scoring per auditing-cc-configs/scripts/verdict_compute.py); reviewer output drives humans; PV output drives gate decisions. Forcing convergence destroys audience-fit.
Bridge table is purely additive — no migration cost on existing audit outputs, reviewer outputs, or PV outputs.
Lowest migration cost: no skill family rewrites; no schema rewrites in audit-issues.json.
Externally undecided (no T-corroborator) means we should prefer the lowest-irreversibility option.
cons: Three vocabularies stay in the repo; readers must consult the bridge to translate.
Risk of bridge becoming stale if any of the three vocabularies evolves independently.
Single-sourced support: claim C-0108 is the only direct claim on this; no T-001..T-004 corroborator.
Translator semantics are non-trivial (NIT vs recommended vs informational are not strictly equivalent).
preconditions: Bridge table host file authored (KB-review-disciplines/severity-taxonomy.md is the canonical-host candidate per framer).
auditing-shared utility (optional) to mechanically translate one vocab to another at audit-issues.json emission time.
design-composer ratifies the bridge (because it cross-cuts layers).

cost.maintenance_burden: moderate (bridge stays in sync as any one vocabulary evolves)
cost.irreversibility_cost: low (additive; can be replaced by canonicalize-with-translator later if scope justifies)

options.name: canonicalize_with_translator
options.description: Pick auditor BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR/NIT as canonical (most populous; widest in-repo footprint per the auditing-mcp / auditing-cc-configs / auditing-shared surfaces). Reviewer and PV vocabularies map to canonical via a documented translator (e.g., auditing-shared utility).
pros: Single canonical vocabulary for tooling; downstream consumers (audit-issues.json schema, verdict_compute.py) target one set of values.
Translator is mechanical — once authored, the human cost is one-time.
cons: Reviewer output and PV output must run through the translator at emission time — touches three skill families.
Translator semantics are non-trivial: BLOCKER → critical → blocking is monotonic only for the worst severities; NIT/recommended/informational are not strictly equivalent.
Migration cost touches KB-review-disciplines, test-phase-validator-author, shared-document-reviewer — wider blast radius than the bridge-table option.
Forces the reviewer audience (humans) to consume canonical vocabulary indirectly, which may obscure intent.
evidence_anchors: C-0094/C-0097/C-0098/C-0101 (auditor vocab is widest in-repo footprint)
preconditions: Translator hosted in auditing-shared.
Three audit surfaces migrated to emit-via-translator.

cost.irreversibility_cost: high (one-way per framer — undoing means restoring three separate emission paths)

options.note: Defensible if design-composer prioritises canonical tooling input over audience-fit. Not recommended because the irreversibility cost is high, the audience-fit cost is real (humans don't naturally read BLOCKER on review output), and the externally-undecided status counsels reversibility.

options.name: unify_one_vocabulary_across_all_surfaces
options.description: Pick one vocabulary (whichever) and migrate auditor + reviewer + PV surfaces to it. Single canonical set; no bridge; no translator.
pros: Maximum simplicity in steady state.
Single audit-issues.json schema; single severity column everywhere.
cons: Highest migration cost: touches at minimum auditing-mcp, auditing-subagents, auditing-cc-configs, auditing-shared, KB-review-disciplines, test-phase-validator-author, shared-document-reviewer.
Destroys audience-fit: humans on review output and gate-decision PV authors lose vocabulary tailored to their use.
One-way per framer: high irreversibility cost.
Externally undecided (no T-corroborator); largest-blast-radius option has the weakest evidence.

cost.maintenance_burden: low in steady state but high migration cost

options.rejection_rationale: Highest cost; widest blast radius; weakest evidence; destroys audience-fit. Externally-undecided + one-way + tenant-blast-radius is the worst configuration for forcing convergence.

mappings.rationale: Three vocabularies serve three different surfaces (tooling, humans, gates). Externally-undecided + one-way + tenant-blast-radius counsels the lowest-irreversibility option that still solves the cross-surface translation problem. Bridge table is additive; design-composer authors it. The two heavier options remain admissible if observed audit-output usage justifies the migration cost in a later iteration.
loss_summary: pattern_fidelity: none (each surface preserves its idiom)
mappings.deferred_to: design-composer ratifies the bridge wording (cross-cuts layers); design-cc proposes the bridge for the cc layer.
